what: The upper bound on the domain feed: the question it answers, the answer the question gives, the answer the frame gives, and the gap between them.
whyThisFileExists: Issue #128 asked only 'how many lines fit', got four, and a technical limit silently became a product result. Issue #145 forbids repeating that. So the question is asked first, its answer is written down even though it does not fit, and the wall is measured rather than assumed.
theQuestion: How many lines does it take to read what is happening in the domain?

answerFromTheQuestion.reasoning: The domain is its creatures, and what a player must be able to read without clicking is which of them something happened to and what it was. One line per creature is the shape of that answer.
answerFromTheQuestion.measured: On the shipped baseline party at tick 2400 all 9 creatures have had something that mattered.
answerFromTheQuestion.howToReadThatRun: It prints one line per creature of the baseline party at tick 2400 — '<name>: <routine> of <entries> (<share>%)'. All nine lines have entries > routine, which is 'something that mattered' for every one of them.
answerFromTheQuestion.correction: An earlier version of this file named the DomainFeedTests run as the source of this number and of two others — '50 distinct who-and-what beats' and '11 distinct kinds'. That run prints neither. The two numbers came from a throwaway probe, nothing reproduces them and nothing reads them, so they are removed rather than re-sourced: they decorated a decision the reasoning above already carries. Found by independent review of PR #152.
answerFromTheQuestion.howMuchOfTheJournalMattered: 155 of 4425 entries at tick 2400. Printed by the DomainFeedTests run (the per-window report line) and carried on the panel's own header.

answerFromTheFrame.whatActuallyBinds: The sentences, not the header — which is the thing this issue got wrong first and had to measure. A turning point carries its numbers with it ('Мотылёк broke and ran: 79% health, 5 raiders close, 0 ally down.') and three of those need SEVEN drawn lines in a 287-pixel column, where three routine sentences needed six. The old feed showed the newest three entries, and the newest three are routine, so it never paid for that. The header is one drawn line at 51 characters and was never the constraint: measured by shortening it to 39 and then to 28 characters, both of which left the panel needing the same 11 lines.
answerFromTheFrame.arithmetic: header 1 + three turning-point sentences 7 + blank line 1 + diagnostics counter 1 = exactly 10 of the 10 the label holds at the tightest frame the guard checks.
answerFromTheFrame.whatThisIssuePaidWithIt: The diagnostics counter used to read 'Diagnostics: 0 (structured JSON is emitted by smoke/capture).', which wraps onto two drawn lines. With the note the panel measured 11 of 10 and the screenshots stage failed; with the note moved into the HudText.Feedback docstring and the count kept, it is 10 of 10. The alternatives are listed under theGap.whatWasNotDoneAboutIt.

howItWasMeasured.mutation: HudText.DomainFeedLines raised from 3 to 4, nothing else changed.
howItWasMeasured.resultAtFour: verification_result status error, failedPhase stage, failedStage godot
howItWasMeasured.messageAtFour: The HUD loses text in 1 place(s): 'feedback' needs 11 lines but only 10 fit in (287, 200) at viewport (2048, 1440), UI scale 2.
howItWasMeasured.resultAtThree: the full nine-stage run is ok: verification_result status ok, scope full, stagesExecuted [scripts, build, tests, mcp, sim, load, godot, ui, screenshots]
howItWasMeasured.beforeTheDiagnosticsNoteWasTrimmed: at THREE lines the same command reported 'feedback' needs 11 lines but only 10 fit at the same frame, and the failing stage was screenshots, on the prepared party at tick 1670 and on baseline at tick 2400. That run is what turned the arithmetic above from a guess into a measurement.
howItWasMeasured.whichLabel: the live 'feedback' label, not a padded worst case. Main.CreatureStoryPanels pads the story shape; the domain feed is measured as the panel the entry point actually carries, which is why raising the constant is enough to redden it.

answerFromTheFrame.slack: zero on the shape that carries turning points, exactly as for the story panel at four lines. That is the right failure — loud rather than silent — but it is a second HUD panel with no headroom and it belongs in the debt ledger beside the first.

whichStageHoldsIt.claim: The two stages that measure this panel do not hold the same thing, and only one of them holds the ceiling.
whichStageHoldsIt.godot: reads the feed at ticks 1 and 190, where every line is routine and the panel is 9 drawn lines of 10. It has a whole line of slack and stays green through the next longer routine sentence.
whichStageHoldsIt.screenshots: the only input inside verify.ps1 where the feed carries turning points: the prepared party at tick 1670. There the panel is 10 of 10.

howItWasMeasured.probe: one drawn line put back into the panel — the diagnostics counter temporarily restored to 'Diagnostics: {n} (structured JSON is emitted by smoke/capture).', nothing else changed
howItWasMeasured.godotResult: verification_stage status ok, stage godot, elapsedSeconds 29.9
howItWasMeasured.screenshotsResult: verification_result status error, failedStage screenshots; 'The HUD loses text in 1 place(s): 'feedback' needs 11 lines but only 10 fit in (287, 200) at viewport (2048, 1440), UI scale 2.' The two baseline t1 captures of that stage passed; the prepared t1670 capture is the one that failed.
howItWasMeasured.secondReading: consistent with the bound mutant above: at DomainFeedLines = 4 the godot stage itself reports 11 needed, which is header 1 + four routine sentences at 2 drawn lines each + blank 1 + counter 1. Three routine sentences is therefore 9.

whichStageHoldsIt.whichStageGuardsWhat: They catch different mistakes. Raising DomainFeedLines adds two drawn lines and godot catches it on its own — that is the bound mutant. Lengthening a sentence adds one, and only screenshots catches that.
whichStageHoldsIt.practicalConsequence: Whoever lengthens an EventNarration sentence next must run the screenshots stage, or the full verify.ps1. `-Stage godot` alone will pass and the feed will ship a line short.
whichStageHoldsIt.correction: The first version of this file, of the HudText.DomainFeedLines docstring and of contract 11.1 all said the godot stage holds this bound. That was wrong, and this same file contradicted it two keys away in howItWasMeasured.beforeTheDiagnosticsNoteWasTrimmed, which records screenshots as the stage that actually failed. Found by independent review of PR #152; the cost of leaving it was that Issue #145's own 'known limitation' instructs the next implementer to run -Stage godot and would have handed them a green run on a truncated panel.

theGap.what: Six of the nine crew are not on the panel, and neither are the earlier beats of the three that are.
whereItIsSaid: in the product: the header reads 'EVENT FEEDBACK · 3 of 9 crew · 155 of 4425 mattered', so the panel never claims to be the domain
in the code: the HudText.DomainFeedLines docstring states the question, both answers and the gap
for the player: one click puts any creature's own four beats on the same panel (HudText.CreatureStory)
whatWasNotDoneAboutIt: The panel is not made taller. Its height is Main.cs arithmetic, and Main.cs is held by another task this block (#147).

The sentences are not shortened. EventNarration is shared by the feed, the story panel, the inspector and the map, so shortening it for the feed's budget would move wording nobody asked to change — and the debt ledger already records that the story panel has zero slack at four lines, so a shorter sentence would be spent there first. This is the cheapest remaining line to buy if the feed is ever worth four.

The blank line between the feed and the diagnostics counter is kept. Dropping it would buy a tenth line of slack and cost the only visual separation between what the crew did and a developer's counter. The count was trimmed instead, which buys the same line and costs a note nobody reads twice.

theThreshold.what: The share of sampled feed windows that must carry at least one entry that mattered.
theThreshold.whyThatNumber: The ceiling on this party is 45.8% — 22 of the 48 sampled windows are taken at a moment when the party has produced anything that mattered at all, and the first ~1300 ticks of a baseline party have none. A floor of 100% would be a claim about the party rather than about the panel. The claim with no slack in it is stated separately and is 100% of the windows where it applies: DomainFeedTests.The_feed_carries_something_that_mattered_whenever_the_party_has_one.
